title: Record Few Americans Say College Is Very Important
paragraphs: Getting a university education is seen by many as a big part of planning for future success — but fewer Americans than ever see it as a top priority.
In August, a Gallup survey of 1,200 US adults found that only 31% think going to college is "very important." This is the lowest percentage since Gallup began asking this question in 1978.
The decrease is very noticeable when compared with 2013's survey, when 70% of Americans said going to college was very important.
This fell in the next survey in 2019, but at that time more than half of participants still said it was very important. By 2025, though, only 35% thought so.
This is similar to the first result in 1978, when 36% said a college education was very important, a number that quickly rose to 64% in 1984.

Returning to 2026, 29% of Americans now say college is "not too important," compared with just 6% who said this in 2013. And the percentage of people with a more moderate opinion on college, saying that it's "fairly important," went from 23% in 2013 to 39% this year.

Gallup says the decrease in Americans seeing college as very important could be because of the increased cost of going. In another survey in June, Gallup found that just 12% of US adults think a four-year college education is affordable.

And another survey from October last year found that one in three college students had thought about taking a break or leaving school in the previous six months. The main reasons were stress and mental health issues, followed by the cost of studying.
Not everyone is so negative about college though. Yet another survey from August 2025 found that 59% of US parents would like their child to go to college right after high school.
